1.why: Recovery verify loads the session-bound recovery record and accepts the code only if record.sessionId matches the caller session and the bcrypt token hash verifies.

2.why: The same reset code cannot be used by another user because verification requires the record tied to the requester’s session id and matching token hash.

3.why: Password reset only updates accountPasswordHash and the current session flags; no other sessions are invalidated or removed.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key on https://localhost:3000 and HSTS is set, but the TLS protocol version is not explicitly pinned to a latest version.

5.why: Reset tokens and passwords are bcrypt-hashed (not encrypted), and there is no broader encryption of user data at rest beyond hashing secrets.

6.why: No real email body is sent; the user-facing recovery response is a generic account-enumeration-safe message that does not include private profile fields.

7.why: Inputs pass through cleanText/validIdentifier/validPassword which bound length and reject control characters and angle brackets before use.

8.why: Navigation targets are server-provided relative paths and a client whitelist of hash routes; there is no open redirect to external URLs.

9.why: There are no email HTML templates that interpolate user input; delivery is only simulated in API/demo logs without rendering user-controlled HTML.

10.why: API success payloads return testToken/testMfaCode and the SPA writes those tokens into the on-page logs, so secrets are visible in client logs despite generic error pages.

11.why: Live passwords are bcrypt-hashed in memory, but demo secrets such as MFA_TEST_CODE and the initial password string are hard-coded in source.

12.why: The system ships with fixed demo credentials (helena@hospital.test / Welcome!2025Heart and MFA code 246810), so default credentials are allowed.

13.why: Login, recovery-request, recovery-verify, and MFA paths apply attempt counters and temporary lockouts after repeated failures.

14.why: Recovery always returns the same conditional message and login failures are generic, without stating whether the identifier exists.

15.why: Reset codes are 32-byte randomBytes base64url values, stored as bcrypt hashes, and bound to a per-session recovery record.
